sections.html:
Pembroke Pines lies in southwest Broward and counts more than 170,000 residents. Major highways, jobs, parks and golf courses are all close. On January 16, 1960 it incorporated as the Village of Pembroke Pines, home to about 1,500 people. Hurricane Andrew in 1992 set off a building rush that made it one of the fastest growing cities in the country, so a large share of its housing dates from the 1990s or later.

Families drawn to schools and parks make up much of the buyer pool, along with residents of the Century Village area. Your home's age is a good first clue to whether a cash offer or a listing suits you better.

sections.h2: House age by side of town
sections.html:
The city annexed land west of US 27 by 1981, so the age of a house depends on which side of town it stands. Fire Station 79 opened in 1981 on that annexed land, and Station 89 followed in 1986 at Century Village.

  • Find out how old your roof, wiring and plumbing are.
  • Ask a title agent to list recorded items on your lot.
  • Keep permit and inspection records where a buyer's inspector can see them.

sections.h2: What Florida charges to transfer a house
sections.html:
Stamp tax on a deed is 70 cents for each $100 of consideration, and everyone on the document answers for it.

Which documents carry stamp tax on a real estate transfer
DocumentStamp tax applies?
Warranty deedYes
Quit claim deedYes
Deed in lieu of foreclosure saleYes
Personal representative deed under probated willNot taxable

The clerk of court collects when the deed is recorded. Have your closing agent work out the amount on your price and give it to you in writing.

Broward's property appraiser sets value as of January 1 and accepts exemption filings until March 1. The office phone is 954-357-6830.

  • A proposed tax notice comes in August.
  • Bills paid in November get the biggest discount, 4 percent.
  • Anything unpaid on April 1 is delinquent.

At closing, the year's tax is divided between you and the buyer. Make sure the division respects your exemption status.

sections.h2: Homestead and portability if you move
sections.html:
Long-time owners benefit most. Save Our Homes limits yearly assessment increases to 3 percent or CPI, whichever is lower, and the savings built up, up to $500,000, can be ported to a Florida home you buy next.

Begin the new homestead inside three years of the January 1 that follows giving up the old one, and send Form DR-501T along with the DR-501 by March 1. Amendments passed later reach the 2027 roll first, so ask the appraiser which rules apply today.

Three situations here come with deadlines. For an estate, summary administration is possible when non-exempt assets total $150,000 or less. Creditors must file by three months after publication or 30 days after service, whichever ends later. Once a foreclosure judgment is entered, the sale arrives 20 to 35 days afterward.

Collect your documents first, because every one of these facts changes the offers you will get.

Fire rescue here began as a volunteer group in 1953, hired three full-time employees in 1973 and now works from six stations. In 2014 the city became the South Region answering point for the Broward County Regional 911 system. Buyers ask about response times and insurance ratings, so find out from your insurer what rating your address gets and keep the answer with your sale papers.

Tax not paid by April 1 goes delinquent, and certificates are offered by June 1. When two years have gone by, the holder may pay $75 to apply for a tax deed, which leads to a clerk's auction.

On a homestead, the opening bid is one half of the latest assessed value plus what is owed. A seller who is behind can ask the Broward tax collector for a payoff figure and may do better selling before a deed application.

  • To pay in installments, file the application by May 1.
  • Seniors can defer on Form DR-570, due March 31.

sections.h2: What buyers ask about the city
sections.html:
The city lists 41 arts and cultural facilities along with parks, golf courses and tree-lined neighborhoods, and it has been recognized as an All-America City. Its stated mission is a place to live, work and raise a family, so lead with those points when you describe the neighborhood. Fire Station 69 opened in 1978 and Station 101 came in 2001 with a communications center, which gives a buyer a sense of how long the area has had full-time coverage.

Mention anything that is true of your street, such as a nearby park, a golf course view or a quiet cul-de-sac, and keep it factual. Buyers check a map, so a plain description beats an inflated one.

Owners past 65 can claim up to $50,000 more if the local ordinance permits and income is low enough. A disabled veteran gets $5,000 off assessed value, and an older owner with a service-connected disability may get a discount matching the VA percentage.

Deployed servicemembers may get an exemption in proportion to time away and can rent out the house without losing homestead. Ask the appraiser's office about proof. The buyer does not inherit any of these breaks.

Giving someone legal or beneficial title counts as a change of ownership for assessment, apart from spouse transfers and some transfers at death. A quit claim deed also draws stamp tax. Florida wants the conveyance in writing and signed before two witnesses, so a title agent should draw it up.

A cash buyer needs no loan, so the lender's appraisal and weeks of underwriting drop away. Clear title, a signed deed and a closing agent to record it are still required. Before agreeing, have the closing date and as-is terms written down, decide who pays stamps and recording, and ask if the buyer will assume an association balance or an open permit.

Any mortgage balance is paid from your proceeds, with the closing agent getting the final figure from your lender. If association dues are overdue, request a statement so the balance is cleared at closing and not discovered afterward.

Having a tenant need not stop a sale, though the lease controls your timing. Unpaid rent draws a 3 day notice, and many fixable breaches get 7 days. A sale does not end a lease, so read it before listing and show buyers the rent record early. Investors often buy with a tenant in place, which can spare you the wait.

Once you accept, the title agent searches the record, collects payoffs and drafts the deed for two witnesses to sign. The clerk records it and takes the tax.

  • Name the stamp payer in the contract.
  • Order mortgage payoff and association statements.
  • Check your exemption status before the tax split.
  • Have permit and inspection records ready for the buyer's inspector.

Begin with paperwork: the deed, the newest tax bill, any association papers, and permit records for roofs, windows or additions. Then compare a listing, a private sale and a cash offer by what you net, and insist on a written offer you have read line by line. With a cash buyer, get the closing date in writing and confirm the house is taken as is, so no repair requests show up after inspection. Nearby sales are easy to compare in a city this size, so get a short list from an agent before you set a price.

faqs.a: January 16, 1960, when it was a village of about 1,500 people.

faqs.q: What doc stamp rate applies to a Pembroke Pines deed?
faqs.a: 70 cents per $100 of consideration, the same rate countywide.

faqs.q: Can I carry my Save Our Homes savings to a new house?
faqs.a: Possibly, if you start a new Florida homestead within three years. Portability can carry up to $500,000 of the difference.
State rules make each party liable, so the contract should name who pays.

faqs.q: Is an inherited house taxed when it transfers?
faqs.a: Not when a personal representative signs under a probated will. Other transfers may be taxed, so ask a title agent.
